description: Breadth-first search (BFS) explores a state space level by level from the start: first all states one step away, then all states two steps away, and so on. It keeps the frontier in a first-in, first-out queue and visits each state at most once. So the first goal it reaches has the fewest steps of all paths to a goal. BFS is complete on finite spaces and optimal in the number of steps, but it ignores action costs; when steps have different costs, use Dijkstra's algorithm or A*.
